newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-AMEC CEO hopes for div growth H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-AMEC CEO hopes for div growth H2.

text.p: AMEC Plc, the UK building and engineering group, said on Thursday it hoped to raise the final dividend payout, pointing to upbeat expectations for the second half after announcing a doubling of first half profits.

AMEC chief executive Peter Mason told Reuters "We would hope to improve the dividend at the year end," after freezing the interim payout at 1.5 pence per share. Mason also said he aimed to boost Amec's international position through acquisitions and partnerships, raising overseas sales to 50 percent of total turnover from the current 30 percent in the long term.
AMEC's first half profits doubled to 12.1 million stg from 6.1 million in the six months to June 30, with turnover at 1.32 billion, up from 1.13 billion.
Despite the strong peformance, Mason told Reuters that the board had decided to maintain its dividend at 1.5 pence.
"On balance we felt it was better to have a dividend which was covered rather than try for a small increase. But we will deal with it properly at the year end," he said.
He added that he was confident that profits would be better than last year after announcing in the results that turnover should hit the stated target of 2.75 billion stg.
Commenting on his stategic review which was kicked off seven months ago, Mason said that it was crucial for AMEC to diversify abroad.
"Long term we need to get 50 percent of our business from outside the UK, up from the current 30 percent," he said.
He added that "all options are open," though he sees a number of small deals rather than a big acquisition.
"I see no merit in acquisitions in basic building or civil engineering businesses, but I want companies offering value-added technology and design."
A number of deals are currently under discussion, he said.
The order book for the group currently stands at 2.8 billion stg. Looking at a breakdown of the results, the mechanical and electrical businesses saw a 20 percent rise in turnover.

Building and civil engineering saw turnover up 28 percent but the result was held back by a poor performance in West Germany which has been hit by low government infrastructure spending and difficult market conditions.

Mason said it was in contrast to brisker business in Eastern Germany. He said that as a result AMEC is seeking to switch some of its operations from west to east Germany, but the process is likely to be a difficult and drawn out one.
Asked whether he saw an improvement soon in West Germany he said "No I don't see an improvement soon."

In the process and energy unit which bounced back into profit in 1996, Mason said the financial benefits of the rationalisation which has taken place will feed through in 1997 resulting in "noticably better" profits for the period.
The housing division's sales were up 11 percent.
Following a failed takeover bid at the end of 1995, Norway's Kvaerner ASA holds a 26 percent stake in AMEC which it has said it is unlikely to retain in the medium term.
